preset.process: AI for Science and Collaborative EU Projects Access
preset.reference_title: EuroHPC JU Call for Proposals for AI for Science and Collaborative EU Projects
preset.summary: Access for AI-driven science and EU-funded collaborative projects, evaluated after each cut-off.

call.name: AI for Science and Collaborative EU Projects Access
call.description: Access for scientific research that relies on AI models, continuously open with cut-offs. Proposals are evaluated together after each cut-off: administrative check, technical assessment per partition, two expert evaluations, an optional consensus report, and the allocation decision on a first-come-first-served basis before the applicant accepts the award.

proposal_roles.name: Consensus expert
proposal_roles.description: One of the experts who reviewed the proposal, whom the call managers ask to consolidate the two expert evaluations when their scores diverge.

workflow_steps.name: Administrative check
workflow_steps.description: The call managers check the online submission form and the Project Scope and Plan document for administrative inconsistencies within a week of the cut-off. An ineligible proposal is rejected and may be resubmitted to a later cut-off.

workflow_steps.name: Technical assessment
workflow_steps.description: The team of each requested partition (the hosting entity's computing centre representative or a technical reviewer they delegate to) assesses whether the proposal can run there: accepted or rejected. A proposal rejected on any partition is not awarded.

workflow_steps.name: Expert evaluation
workflow_steps.description: The call managers assign or invite two independent experts, who confirm having no conflict of interest and evaluate the proposal against the three criteria without seeing each other's evaluations. Proposals scoring below the call's quality threshold, set on the allocation decision, cannot be awarded: the consensus grading counts when one was made, else the experts' average.

call_team.active: Under Expert Evaluation - {invited} experts invited, {accepted} accepted, {declined} declined, {submitted} evaluations submitted

criteria.name: Quality and efficiency of the implementation

workflow_steps.name: Consensus report
workflow_steps.description: Runs only where the two experts' scores lie more than one point apart: the call managers assign a consensus expert, who confirms having no conflict of interest and consolidates the two evaluations into an agreed grading. Where the scores agree the proposal skips the step and nobody is notified.

workflow_steps.name: Resources allocation decision
workflow_steps.description: Use Allocate in submission order on the round once every proposal has reached this step: proposals are awarded first come first served until the cut-off's budgets are depleted, and those below the quality threshold are declined. Proposals can also be decided one by one. Set the cut-off's budgets on the call; the results are communicated to all applicants together when the round's results are published.

workflow_steps.name: Award response
workflow_steps.description: The applicant accepts or declines the award before resources are created.

workflow_steps.name: Extension request
workflow_steps.description: An awarded applicant asks to extend the project: the circumstances and the resource usage so far, the new end date and the resources needed. Asked at the latest one month before the project ends.

workflow_steps.name: Extension request assessment
workflow_steps.description: The team of each partition hosting the project assesses whether the extension is valid and can be accepted: accepted, conditionally accepted or rejected. Only a partition whose team accepts takes the extension.

workflow_steps.name: Extension request results
workflow_steps.description: The call managers decide the extension following the assessment: the end date and resources granted. An approved extension moves the project's end date; more resources are ordered from the partitions, whose providers approve the orders as usual.

workflow_steps.name: Final report
workflow_steps.description: The awarded applicant submits the project's final report. The step opens at the end of the allocation period, an extension included.

workflow_steps.name: Final report approval
workflow_steps.description: The call managers approve the final report, which completes the project.

checklists.name: Consensus report
checklists.description: The consensus expert's consolidation of the two expert evaluations.

questions.description: Score: Quality and efficiency of the implementation

checklists.description: Why an awarded project needs more time or resources.

Summarise how the allocated resources have been used up to now on each partition.

checklists.name: Final report
checklists.description: The results of an awarded project once its allocation ends.

questions.user_guidance: Report what the project achieved with the allocated resources, including publications and outcomes.
Optional. One PDF file with the full report.

scenarios.name: Happy path
scenarios.description: Every step passes and the applicant accepts the award.

scenarios.name: Rejected at the administrative check
scenarios.description: The office finds the proposal ineligible: it is rejected, the applicant is told and no other step runs.

scenarios.name: Changes requested at the administrative check
scenarios.description: The office asks for changes, the applicant submits them and the proposal is then found eligible; the technical assessment starts.

actions.message: Please complete the Project Scope and Plan.

scenarios.name: Extension and final report
scenarios.description: After the award the applicant team asks for an extension, the partitions accept it and it is approved; at the end the final report is submitted and approved.

scenarios.name: Rejected at the technical assessment
scenarios.description: A partition rejects the proposal: it is not awarded.

scenarios.name: Expert scores diverge
scenarios.description: The two experts score the proposal 2 and 5: more than a point apart, so the consensus report runs, a consensus expert consolidates the evaluations and the proposal goes on to the allocation decision.

scenarios.name: Expert scores agree
scenarios.description: The two experts score the proposal 4 and 5: within a point, so the proposal skips the consensus report, nobody is told about it, and the allocation decision follows the expert evaluation.
